output.title: Late payment terms are a workflow problem, not just finance
output.body:
Late payment terms usually show up as a workflow problem before they show up as a finance problem. For an owner-operator, the bounded question is not “are the terms bad?” but “which recurring step is causing the drag: invoice tracking, payment-chasing emails, or an aging report in a spreadsheet?” That is the decision worth looking at first.

If the workflow is repeatable, measurable, and mostly the same each time, it may be a candidate for AI or workflow automation. If it changes too much from case to case, or if the step touches money movement or another high-risk decision, keep human approval in place and leave that part manual. That is not a failure; it is control.

Bareni’s normal sequence is a free diagnostic, then a one-page pilot proposal, then a working MVP if the workflow fits. Those timings are intended scopes, not guarantees, and the diagnostic can also say plainly that AI is not the right tool.

A practical next step is simple: write down the last five overdue-payment cases and ask one question about each one — was the follow-up the same every time? If yes, you have a workflow to examine. If no, you have a judgment call that stays human. Dry, but useful.
